content: A cage bed is a type of bed that is equipped with either metal bars or netting, specifically designed to confine an individual within the boundaries of the bed. This form of restraint is often used in psychiatric settings to prevent patients from harming themselves or others. In the Czech Republic, psychiatric practitioners have persistently defended the use of cage beds, arguing that they represent the most effective method of restraint in certain situations. Jan Slezak, the director of the Social Care Home in Raby, located in eastern Bohemia, has stated, We can either use cage beds, or we can increase patients' medication, strap them down, or place them in solitary confinement. He further emphasized, We see cage beds as the best solution. Efforts to ban the use of cage beds in the Czech Republic gained significant attention through a political campaign that was notably supported and popularized by the author J.K. Rowling.
